title: The same-hand ed–od contrast has one Currier A leaf in the public material
statement: The sole overlapping hand and section in ZL, IT and RF is hand 3 in section S. Both public partitions use one Currier A leaf, f58 in quire 8, and all B leaves are in quire 20. The public practice pages reuse training leaves on both sides. ZL exact one-site ed/od counts are 1/8 versus 1312/234 in training and 3/6 versus 143/31 in practice. The open-curve and loop sequence at f58r.15 is visually consistent with ed across all three transcriptions. The unusual sign at f58r.23 is encoded as d in ZL and IT and as extended EVA in RF.
check: Treat the hand 3 contrast as descriptive until there are independently attributed physical A and B leaves in the same hand and section, with quire overlap. Retain the frozen exact pairs, check the same visible loci across transcriptions, and keep entire physical leaves out of the training inventory before claiming replication. Any claim about writing order needs direction evidence from material or scribal analysis.
protocol:
# P-L1-023 spelling comparison on physical leaves

Use the pinned ZL, IT and RF public practice split, with its training complement and its public evaluation pages reported separately. ZL physical metadata supply the same folio number (recto, verso and panels), quire and bifolium identifier for all three transcriptions. Cross-check the physical inventory against the archived bifolium comparison source. Only paragraph word tokens enter the lexical analysis. Work on certain words with the default tokenizer and report a joined-uncertain-space sensitivity. A word with ed or od anywhere counts once for each corresponding literal predicate. Transcriptions of the same physical leaves are alternative readings, not independent specimens.

Freeze the four published Timm pairs as [chedy, chody], [chedar, chodar], [chedal, chodal], [qokeedy, qokeody]. For a general one-site variant, require exactly one literal ed-or-od position in the word and existence of both spellings after substituting only its first letter. Freeze that vocabulary separately per transcription in the public training inventory, pooled over Currier groups before using A/B labels or evaluation words. Retain the default-tokenizer vocabulary for the alternate-space run. For each one-site family report a common-context ED/(ED+OD) weighted by token volume, and show the published pairs individually. New evaluation words cannot add families.

Inventory nonempty certain paragraph pages and unique physical leaves, bifolia, and quires per section, attributed hand and Currier group. Identify exact same-hand, same-section A/B overlap in each public partition. For independent-group inference require at least two physical A-only and two B-only bifolia per cell and enough quire overlap to separate quire and Currier effects. A shared-sheet comparison is counted only when two distinct folio leaves on the same bifolium supply opposite labels within the same hand and section. Describe rates where support fails, with no token-level confidence intervals or tests. Whole-bifolium and whole-quire deletions show the sensitivity of pooled descriptive differences. They do not supply matched effects when a group disappears.

Image review targets the eligible A-side public training ed loci in the only hand-section overlap and records exact locus, alternative transcription, and visual uncertainty. Sequence of binding, leaf adjacency, folio numbers or Currier written labels are not direction indicators for writing. Require independent relevant dated or superposition evidence for an A-before-B conclusion. No secret pages or retained assignments outside the public split are used.

physical_audit_notes: The pinned map describes 102 leaves and 42 numbered panels on 10 leaves. All 50 represented mate pairs agree with the immutable external map; 58 rows there include also missing leaves.

The training comparison is f58r vs 19 B pages on 12 leaves/six sheets. The practice comparison is f58v vs f107r, f111v, f113r on three B sheets. Every practice leaf used in this cell has its other face in training.

Quire 8 vs quire 20 is perfectly confounded with A vs B in the only matching cell. There is no same-quire or same-sheet A/B pair. Present gathering sequence, later foliation, signs of rebinding, and quire marks do not independently date the ink on f58 relative to quire 20.
The f58 mate f65 has another section and no A/B label in the pinned metadata. No numbered panel is in the matching cell.
The later lines of mixed-hand f115r add 331, 324 and 320 training B tokens in ZL, IT and RF under the reviewed partial attribution. The counts of B leaves, sheets and quires are unchanged.
The full one-site family tables report each spelling in both dialects. Pooled exact-family rates can still shift because the mix of eligible families differs between dialect groups.
Pooled leave-one-bifolium and leave-one-quire ranges only measure descriptive sensitivity. A confidence interval whose A-side support is a single leaf does not estimate between-leaf variation.

image_reading.protocol: Two readers inspected the same native Yale crops after seeing the public transcription loci. These are targeted graphic checks, and not blind new transcriptions.

crops.observation: The open curve immediately before the standard looped sign distinguishes this from a closed o.
Two open curves precede a tall looping sign with an extended connector; the sign differs visibly from the shorter loop in the comparison crop. RF uses extended EVA @152, not a missing reading.
The oval before the loop is closed and provides an od comparison in ZL and IT.
An open curve precedes the looped d. This is the verso of the same A leaf.
